full_judgment:
Mr. Md. Delwar Hossain, J:- This Rule upon an application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure was issued calling upon the opposite party to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and order dated 11.4.2007 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, Fifth Court, Dhaka in Miscellaneous Appeal No.93 of 2006 allowing the appeal reversing the judgment and order dated 19.3.2006 passed by the learned Assistant Judge. Second Court and House Rent Controller, Dhaka in House Rent Case No.1 of 2005 allowing the application under order VII Rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure, should not be set aside and/or pass such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 2. The opposite party filed House Rent Case No. I of 2005 on 1.1.2005 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Second Court and House Rent Controller, Dhaka under House Rent Control Act, 1991 against the petitioner praying for directing him to accept rent on granting rent receipt. 

 3. The petitioner appearing in the said case took several adjournments for filing written objection and lastly on 30.10.2005 filed an application under Order VII Rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure for rejection of the application of the said case contending that the case was not maintainable as the opposite party has filed the said case without taking recourse of arbitration pursuant to tenancy agreement. 

 4. The learned Assistant Judge and House Rent Controller hearing the application under Order VII Rule 11 of the Code by his judgment and order dated 19.3.2006 rejected the application of the said case allowing the application under Order VII Rule 11(d) of the of the Code filed by the present petitioner. 

 5. The opposite party being aggrieved by the said judgment and order dated 19.3.2006 preferred Miscellaneous Appeal No.96 of 2006 before the Court of the learned District Judge Dhaka which ultimately on transfer was heard and disposed of by the learned Joint District Judge, High Court Dhaka. He after hearing both parties by his judgment and order dated 11.4.2007 allowed the appeal setting aside those passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Second Court and House Rent Controller. 

 7. None appeared for either of the parties when the matter was taken up for hearing. It is a settled proposition of law that this Court can dispose of the Rule in exercise of its revisional jurisdiction under section 151(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure in the absence of either of the parties or sue moot on perusal of the record. Reference may be made to the case of Safaruddin Vs. Fazlul Haque reported in 49 DLR (AD) 151. 

 8. I have accordingly, perused the judgments and orders passed by both the House Rent Controller and the Appellate Court and the application of the said case at Annexure-A and the application under Order VII Rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure at Annexure-B annexed with the Civil Revision application. 

 10. The proceeding under House Rent Control Act, 1991 is a summary one. The application under the said Act can not be termed as a plaint. What a plaint should contain has been provided by Order VII Rule 11 of the Code. Order VII Rule 11 of the Code prescribed the circumstances when a plaint would be liable to be rejected. In the cause title of the application of the said case, I find provisions of Sections 13 and 28 and relief is prayed for under section 27 of House Rent Control Act, 1991 have been invoked. In such circumstance the application of the said case is not a plaint. The application of the petitioner made under Order VII Rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure for rejection of such application is wholly misconceived. 

 11. Moreover, such summary proceeding demands expeditious disposal without entering into any complicated question of law and technicalities. Without disposing of the case finally, the learned Assistant Judge and House Rent Controller entertained a misconceived application which was not at all maintainable. 

 14. The learned Assistant Judge, Second Court and House Rent Controller, Dhaka is directed to hear and dispose of the House Rent Case No. 1 of 2005 on merit within 6(six) months from the date of receipt of this Order.
